message.reasoning:
I am preparing a JSON timeline of the future of humanity from present day to year 10000. It will contain 25 to 40 events, be an honest forecast, and avoid narrative style.

I will estimate the current year as 2026. The JSON output will contain no text before or after the object.

I will mark humanity's survival in 10000 as uncertain, given the extreme uncertainty of long-term forecasting. The near-term events will focus on AI development, climate change, geopolitical tensions, and space exploration.

Medium-term risks include possible AGI, climate impacts, and biotechnology. Long-term possibilities span space colonization and human evolution. I will place roughly 32 events across the full 8000-year span, keeping them evenly distributed despite greater uncertainty in the distant future.

I am now drafting specific near-term dates. I will place AI systems reaching most cognitive work around 2028 and major climate tipping points around 2032. I am deliberately avoiding overly confident predictions.

I am now mapping out the remaining events. Fusion power and humanoid robots are expected around 2035 and 2045. Sea-level adaptation and life extension will shape 2050 and 2060. Permanent lunar or Martian presence is projected for 2070. AI governance and post-scarcity economics are planned for 2080 and 2150. Genetic engineering and space habitats are set for 2200 and 2300. Cultural divergence or unification is forecast for 2500.

I am now filling in the later events. Asteroid mining is projected for 2800. Human biological form may become optional by 3000. Interstellar probes are expected around 3500. Speciation is possible by 4000. Civilization cycles or continuity may emerge by 5000. Climate recovery is forecast for 6000. Deep space settlement is planned for 7000. Digital or postbiological dominance is projected for 8000. I am still finalizing the remaining events to reach the 25–40 target. I believe humanity will most likely persist in some transformed form through 10000.

I am now drafting the event descriptions. The first two entries specify AI matching human performance in 2027 and military AI deployment in 2030. I am keeping the language factual and avoiding narrative style.

I am now adding the near-term event details. A severe climate-driven disaster in 2033 will kill large numbers and force major policy shifts. Global primary energy will be majority low-carbon by 2036, though fossil fuels remain politically entrenched. World population growth will nearly stall by 2040 as fertility falls below replacement. By 2045, highly capable AI agents will automate a large share of white-collar and logistics work, causing prolonged labor disruption. Average global temperature will sit roughly 1.7–2.2°C above preindustrial by 2050, with locked-in sea-level rise.

I am now finalizing the near-term entries. A first sustained human presence beyond Earth is projected for 2055. Effective aging treatments will widen health inequality by 2065. Gene editing and embryo selection will become routine by 2075, raising ethical conflicts. By 2090, AI systems will design most scientific instruments, drugs, and software, with human researchers largely setting goals and constraints.

I am now adding the mid-term entries. By 2100, coastal megacities will have either retreated or built massive defenses, making climate migration a central geopolitical fact. A durable global governance regime for advanced AI and biotech will either exist by 2150 or fail after a catastrophic near-miss. By 2200, orbital and lunar industry will supply a meaningful fraction of energy-intensive manufacturing. By 2300, human genetic and cybernetic modification will have produced populations with substantially different capabilities and life histories.

Self-sustaining settlements in the Earth-Moon system and possibly on Mars will reduce single-planet extinction risk by 2500. Natural languages and cultures will have diverged or been deliberately standardized by 2800, severing historical continuity with the 21st century. By 3000, most economically important cognition will run on artificial substrates, making biological humans no longer the main productive class. Interstellar probes will have reached nearby star systems and returned data by 3400.

I am now adding the later events. By 4000, descendant civilizations will have experienced at least one collapse and recovery rather than smooth progress. By 4500, Earth's climate and biosphere will have been heavily managed for millennia, leaving wild nature mainly in preserves or reconstructions. By 5000, humanity will be a lineage of biological, augmented, and machine-based populations that may no longer recognize each other as the same species. By 5500, energy use will be dominated by solar and stellar-scale collection in space rather than planetary industry.

By 6000, records of the early third millennium will survive only as specialized scholarship. Expansion beyond the solar system will be slow and intermittent by 6500, with most descendants still living within it. A major natural hazard will be narrowly survived or avoided through technology by 7000. Biological humans in the 21st-century form will be rare or absent by 7500, leaving continuity as cultural and genetic fragments.

I am now adding the final events. By 8000, posthuman or machine-origin polities will alternate long periods of peace with conflict over energy and compute. By 8500, deliberate mind and body redesign will be routine, with identity often copied, branched, or merged. By 9000, the solar system will be extensively engineered, leaving Earth as a preserve, ruin, or ordinary habitat. By 9500, long-term survival will depend on institutions that outlast individual minds by orders of magnitude, some of which will have failed and been replaced.

The timeline now contains 32 events. I have finalized the summary and the JSON metadata. I will use plain ASCII to avoid encoding issues and keep the detail fields honest about uncertainty.

The timeline now contains 30 events, fitting the 25–40 target. I refined the entries to be more honest and less speculative, framing far-future forecasts as low-confidence extrapolations of durable trends. I am now carefully writing the JSON output.
